full_judgment:
(i) Whether Local investigation under Order 26, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure on matters stated in the application for Local investigation is essential and imperative in resolving the controversy and material issue involved in the suit for a decree of recovery of khas possession on declaration of plaintiff-petitioners title over property described in schedule to plaint 

 7. Petitioner of Civil Revision petition as plaintiff impleading sole opposite party as sole defendant laid a suit being Title Suit No. 326 of 1982 for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession of property described in schedule to plaint. Schedule property will be referred to hereinafter as suit property. The suit was, thereafter, renumbered as Title No. 226 of 1985 on transfer to Second Court of Munsif (now Assistant Judge), Dhaka, Opposite party as sole defendant has been contesting the suit on presentation of a written statement. 

 24. Strenuous argument has been pressed into service from the side of plaintiff-petitioner to bring home contention that the suit being declaration of title and recovery of khas possession over suit property it is necessary for the Court to determine the exact position of the property in part particularly towards western side and a Local Investigation is necessary for proper adjudication of the dispute between parties and learned Assistant Judge committed an error in decision occasioning a failure of justice in rejecting the application for Local Investigation. 

 27. Admittedly, the suit is for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession over the suit property. The suit is not for demarcation from Cadastral Survey plot No. 110 of Mouza Tejkunipara from Cadastrul Survey plot No. 935 of Mouza Kafrul. Defendant-opposite party did not challenge the identity of the suit property '03 acres of Cadastral Survey Plot No. 110 of Mouja Tejkunipara is the suit property and that property is well described by boundary.
